entries.title: Picked the engine and wrote the bootstrap prompt in a separate Claude chat
entries.body:
Before any code, a claude.ai conversation compared engines for a phone-first browser jam game and settled on **Phaser 3 from a CDN, no build step**, deployed on Netlify. It also drafted the bootstrap prompt that started the first Claude Code session.

That prompt was cut off when it was pasted: everything after "Placeholder art is drawn in" got lost. The missing rules were added later in the Claude Code session.

*Lightly condensed by Quirin: a superseded GitHub Pages version of the prompt is reduced to a one-line note.*

conversation.q: What's the best framework for a game jam with Claude? I want to run and iterate in the browser, primarily on my phone, maybe also a laptop. Not sure about the engine.
conversation.a:
Phaser, delivered as a single HTML file that pulls Phaser from a CDN, is the best fit.

**Why this combination works**
- **No build step.** One self-contained HTML page, published and opened on the phone right away. Each change is edited and republished to the same link; you reload. No toolchain, no local server, no laptop required.
- **Phaser is well-trodden ground.** Mature, well documented, with lots of example code, so Claude is reliable with it. It covers what jam games need: sprites, tilemaps, arcade physics, tweens, particles, sound, cameras, scene management.
- **It handles phones properly.** Built-in touch/pointer input, and a scale manager that fits and letterboxes the game to any screen.

**Alternatives depending on the game**
- **Plain Canvas / vanilla JS** for very small or abstract games (puzzles, one-button games). Less to learn, but you rebuild basics like collision yourself.
- **KAPLAY** (formerly Kaboom.js) for tiny arcade games; quicker and more playful than Phaser, smaller ecosystem.
- **Three.js** if the game needs to be 3D. Same single-file/CDN workflow, but 3D costs much more jam time.
- **Godot** is a great engine but doesn't fit this workflow: editor on a laptop and a web export for every iteration.

**Tips**
- Design for touch from minute one (tap/swipe, big hit areas, decide portrait vs. landscape early).
- Use generated or placeholder art (shapes, emoji, art drawn in code).
- Iterate in small changes after each playtest.
- Keep state in memory, not browser storage.

conversation.q: Give me a prompt to bootstrap the repo for this with Phaser.
conversation.a: *(First version targeted GitHub Pages; superseded by the Netlify version below.)*

Only a few lines change, since a no-build repo works on Netlify as-is: swap the Pages workflow for a `netlify.toml` (publish = ".", no build command, no-cache headers), update the README note, and drop the Pages setup step.

To connect it in Netlify: "Add new site" → "Import from Git" → pick the repo. It reads netlify.toml, so leave the build command empty. Every push to main deploys to your `*.netlify.app` URL. Pull requests get deploy previews, so a change on a branch can be playtested at its own URL before merging.

conversation.q: Give me a new prompt for the bootstrap.
conversation.a:
**Final bootstrap prompt (paste into Claude Code):**

```
Bootstrap a game jam repo for a mobile-first browser game using Phaser 3, deployed on Netlify.

Constraints:
- No build step, no npm, no bundler. Plain ES modules served as static files.
- Load Phaser from a CDN (jsdelivr, pinned to a specific 3.x version) in index.html.
- Must run as-is on any static host, so use relative paths only.
- Phone is the primary target: touch controls first, keyboard as a bonus on laptop.

Structure:
- index.html: viewport meta (no zoom), full-screen canvas, Phaser script tag, loads src/main.js
- src/main.js: Phaser game config with Scale.FIT + CENTER_BOTH, a fixed logical resolution (portrait 720x1280 unless I say otherwise), arcade physics, and the scene list
- src/scenes/: BootScene (generates placeholder textures in code with Graphics, no image files), MenuScene (tap to start), GameScene (a tiny playable demo: a player that moves toward where you touch or drag, plus something to collect, plus a score), GameOverScene (tap to restart)
- src/config.js: tunable constants (speeds, sizes, colors) in one place, so I can ask for "feel" changes quickly
- assets/: empty folder with a .gitkeep, for later
- netlify.toml: publish = "." with no build command; add a header rule so index.html and src/** are served with Cache-Control: no-cache (so the phone always picks up the latest push)
- README.md: how to play locally (any static server, e.g. `python3 -m http.server`) and a note that Netlify deploys on push

Also create CLAUDE.md with working rules for future sessions:
- Keep it no-build and CDN-only. Don't add npm dependencies.
- Every change must keep the game playable on a phone. Touch input is the primary control scheme.
- Placeholder art is drawn in code unless I provide assets.
- Don't use localStorage for anything important.
- Put tunables in src/config.js, not inline.
- Make small, focused changes and commit each one with a clear message, so I can playtest after every push.
- After each change, tell me in one or two sentences what to test on the phone.

Finally, prevent the usual mobile pitfalls: block pull-to-refresh and double-tap zoom on the canvas, handle multi-touch, and pause the game when the tab is hidden.

When done, commit and push.
```
